distinction:d_epc_weiterbehandlung_wiede.label: Further processing vs. re-establishment of rights
distinction:d_epc_weiterbehandlung_wiede.frage: Which remedy helps after a time limit vis-à-vis the EPO has been missed?
rows: Art. 121 EPC, R. 135 EPC
Art. 122 EPC, R. 136 EPC
Only the applicant
Applicant and proprietor, exceptionally the opponent (G 1/86)
Irrelevant
All due care required by the circumstances
Two months after the communication of the failure to observe a time limit or of the loss of rights
Two months after removal of the cause of non-compliance, at the latest one year after expiry of the time limit; priority: two months after expiry of the priority period
Pay the fee, complete the omitted act
In writing, fee, statement of grounds with the facts made credible, complete the omitted act
Art. 121(4) EPC and R. 135(2) EPC (among others priority, appeal, period for renewal fees with additional fee, translation, missing parts)
All time limits for which further processing is available, and the time limit for re-establishment itself (R. 136(3) EPC)
Takes precedence
Subsidiary
distinction:d_epc_weiterbehandlung_wiede.merksatz: Further processing first (paying the fee is enough); re-establishment only where further processing is ruled out (prove due care).

distinction:d_epc_54_2_54_3.label: State of the art: Art. 54(2) EPC and Art. 54(3) EPC
distinction:d_epc_54_2_54_3.frage: How does prior-published state of the art differ from earlier European applications?
rows: Everything made available to the public, worldwide, in any form
Only European applications (and Euro-PCT applications under R. 165 EPC)
Available before the effective date
Earlier effective date, published on or after the effective date of the later application
What was made available to the public
Whole contents as originally filed
Novelty and inventive step
Novelty only (second sentence of Art. 56 EPC)
Published PCT application always
Only with filing fee and translation (Art. 153(5) EPC, R. 165 EPC)
National prior rights only in national proceedings (Art. 139(2) EPC)
Priority, non-prejudicial disclosure (Art. 55 EPC)
Disclaimer (G 1/03); different claims per state no longer apply since EPC 2000
distinction:d_epc_54_2_54_3.merksatz: Paragraph 2 harms everything, paragraph 3 only novelty – and only with the content as originally filed.

distinction:d_epc_r56_r56a_r139.label: Missing parts, erroneously filed documents, correction (R. 56, 56a and 139 EPC)
distinction:d_epc_r56_r56a_r139.frage: How are gaps and errors in the application documents remedied, and what happens to the filing date?
rows: Parts of the description or drawings are missing
Documents or parts filed erroneously (e.g. a different application)
Obvious error in documents filed
Two months from the date of filing or from the invitation
Two months from the date of filing or from the invitation
No fixed time limit; declaration of priority only under R. 52(3) EPC
Re-dated to the date on which the missing parts are filed
Re-dated to the date on which the correct documents are filed
Unchanged
Completely contained in the priority application, request and copy filed in time (R. 56(3) EPC)
Completely contained in the priority application, request filed in time (R. 56a(4) EPC)
Within one month of notification of the re-dating (R. 56(6) EPC)
Within one month of notification of the re-dating (R. 56a(7) EPC)
No further processing (R. 135(2) EPC)
No further processing (R. 135(2) EPC)
Appeal against refusal
distinction:d_epc_r56_r56a_r139.merksatz: Something missing: R. 56 EPC. Something wrong: R. 56a EPC. An obvious slip: R. 139 EPC – only the first two cost the filing date.
